name: MSP430F2001IPWR
title: MSP430F20x1, MSP430F20x2, MSP430F20x3 ultra-low-power 16-bit mixed-signal microcontrollers
summary: A family of six small 16-bit RISC microcontrollers running from 1.8 V to 3.6 V at up to 16 MHz, with 1 KB or 2 KB of flash, 128 bytes of RAM, a 16-bit two-channel timer, a watchdog, a brownout detector and ten I/O pins. The F20x1 parts add an analog comparator, the F20x2 a 10-bit 200-ksps SAR ADC and a USI serial port, and the F20x3 a 16-bit sigma-delta ADC with PGA and the USI. Current is 220 µA at 1 MHz and 2.2 V active, 0.5 µA in standby and 0.1 µA with only RAM kept; they come in 14-pin TSSOP, 14-pin PDIP and 16-pin QFN.
key_figures: 1.8 V to 3.6 V (2.2 V for flash writes)
16 MHz max at VCC ≥ 3.3 V; 62.5 ns instruction cycle
1 KB or 2 KB flash + 256 B information flash, 128 B RAM

notes: The 256B is information memory, in addition to the main flash.

tables.title: Interrupt sources
rows: Power-up, external reset, Watchdog Timer+, flash key violation, PC out-of-range
NMI, oscillator fault, flash memory access violation
notes: A PC out-of-range reset occurs when the CPU fetches an instruction from the peripheral register space (0h to 01FFh) or from an unused address range.
(non)-maskable: the interrupt's own enable bit can disable it; the general interrupt enable (GIE) cannot.
Several of these vectors serve more than one flag; the flags of the peripheral sources sit in the peripheral modules.
Vectors 0FFDEh to 0FFC0h are unused on these parts and may hold ordinary program code.

tables.title: Interrupt enable register 1 (address 00h)
rows: Watchdog interrupt enable; active only with the watchdog in interval-timer mode
notes: rw-0: readable and writable, cleared by PUC. Bits 7, 6, 3 and 2 are not implemented. Register 01h (IE2) has no bits on these parts.

tables.title: Interrupt flag register 1 (address 02h)
rows: External reset flag: set by a reset at RST/NMI in reset mode; cleared at VCC power-up
Power-on reset flag: set at VCC power-up
Set on watchdog overflow in watchdog mode or on a security key violation; cleared at VCC power-on or by a reset at RST/NMI in reset mode
notes: rw-0 and rw-1: cleared or set by PUC. rw-(0) and rw-(1): cleared or set by POR. Bits 7 to 5 are not implemented. Register 03h (IFG2) has no bits on these parts.

operation.text: Six parts share the pins and the core: a 16-bit timer, ten I/O and 128 bytes of RAM, with 1 KB (F200x) or 2 KB (F201x) of main flash plus 256 bytes of information flash. The last digit sets the analog block: F20x1 has the Comparator_A+, F20x2 a 10-bit 200-ksps SAR ADC (ADC10) and the USI, F20x3 a 16-bit sigma-delta ADC with differential PGA (SD16_A) and the USI. I versions run from -40°C to 85°C, T versions to 105°C.

A 16-bit RISC core with sixteen 16-bit registers: R0 is the program counter, R1 the stack pointer, R2 the status register (also constant generator 1), R3 constant generator 2, and R4 to R15 are general purpose. A register-to-register operation takes one CPU clock, 62.5 ns at 16 MHz. The instruction set has 51 instructions in three formats; sources have seven addressing modes and destinations four; every instruction works on bytes or words. Peripherals sit on the data, address and control buses and any instruction can reach them.

Active mode runs all clocks. LPM0: CPU and MCLK off, SMCLK and ACLK on. LPM1: as LPM0, and the DCO's dc generator also stops when the DCO is not used in active mode. LPM2: CPU, MCLK and SMCLK off, DCO dc generator on, ACLK on. LPM3: CPU, MCLK, SMCLK and the DCO dc generator off, ACLK on. LPM4: everything off, ACLK and the crystal oscillator included. Any interrupt wakes the part from a low-power mode, runs its handler and can return it to that mode. The DCO restarts in under 1 µs.

Vectors and the reset address occupy 0FFC0h to 0FFFFh, each a 16-bit handler address. If the reset vector at 0FFFEh reads 0FFFFh, as on blank flash, the CPU goes straight into LPM4 after power-up. Power-up, an external reset, the watchdog, a flash key violation and an instruction fetch from the peripheral space (0h to 01FFh) or an unused area all cause a reset.

The brownout circuit holds the part in reset during power-up and power-down. Reset releases when VCC rises through V(B_IT-) + Vhys(B_IT-), never more than 1.8 V, and code starts td(BOR) later. The DCO default must be kept until VCC is high enough for the intended clock frequency. A pulse on RST/NMI must last at least 2 µs to give a reset. Whether a VCC dip trips the brownout depends on both its depth and its width.

The basic clock module has three sources: a 32768-Hz watch crystal on LFXT1, the very-low-power low-frequency oscillator (VLO, 12 kHz typical) and the digitally controlled oscillator (DCO), which starts in under 1 µs. From them it makes ACLK (crystal or VLO), MCLK for the CPU and SMCLK for the peripherals. Calibration constants for 1, 8, 12 and 16 MHz are stored at the factory in information segment A; loading CALBC1_xMHZ into BCSCTL1 and CALDCO_xMHZ into DCOCTL sets the DCO to that frequency. LFXT1Sx = 11 makes XIN a digital clock input.

The highest MCLK frequency rises with VCC: 6 MHz at 1.8 V, 12 MHz at 2.7 V and 16 MHz from 3.3 V, along a straight line between those points. DCO range RSELx = 14 needs 2.2 V or more, RSELx = 15 needs 3.0 V or more. Flash program and erase need at least 2.2 V.

For low EMI on LFXT1: keep the crystal traces short; put a solid ground plane round the oscillator pins; keep other clock and data lines from coupling into XIN and XOUT; route nothing under or beside the XIN and XOUT pins; avoid assembly materials that add parasitic load on them; and make sure any conformal coating adds no leakage between them. XOUT is not to be routed to the JTAG header; the serial programming adapter no longer uses it. The internal load capacitance is chosen with XCAPx (1, 5.5, 8.5 or 11 pF effective).

Flash is programmed through Spy-Bi-Wire or JTAG, or by the CPU in the system with single byte or word writes. Main memory is made of 512-byte segments; information memory is four 64-byte segments, A to D. The main segments can be erased all at once or one at a time; segments A to D one at a time or together with main memory. Segment A carries the calibration data and is locked against program and erase after reset; it can be unlocked, but erasing it loses the calibration. Endurance is 10^4 cycles minimum, retention 100 years at 25°C.

Port P1 has eight bits and port P2 two (P2.6, P2.7). Each bit is set independently as input or output, each can raise an interrupt on a chosen edge, and each has a pullup or pulldown resistor (35 kΩ typical) that can be switched on. All port registers are reachable by every instruction. Outputs drive 6 mA within 0.6 V of the rail, with ±48 mA total for all outputs.
The WDT+ restarts the system when its interval runs out, recovering from a software fault. When not needed it can be stopped, or used as an interval timer that raises interrupts.

Timer_A2 counts in 16 bits and has two capture/compare registers, used for captures, compares, PWM and interval timing. It can interrupt on counter overflow and on each capture/compare register. On the F20x1 the comparator output feeds capture input CCI1B internally; ACLK feeds CCI0B on all parts.

The analog comparator is meant for slope-type A/D conversion, battery supervision and watching external analog signals. Eight pins can be routed to its inputs, its output can be brought out on P1.3 or P1.7, and an internal reference of 0.25 VCC, 0.5 VCC or a diode voltage can be selected. An optional output low-pass filter has a time constant of about 2 µs. Swapping the inputs with CAEX between two readings and summing them removes the offset.

The universal serial interface is shift-register hardware for synchronous serial links such as SPI and I2C. SCLK is on P1.5, SDO/SCL on P1.6, SDI/SDA on P1.7. In I2C mode SDA and SCL pull to within 0.4 V of VSS at 1.5 mA.

A 10-bit SAR converter with sample-and-hold, its own reference generator (1.5 V or 2.5 V) and a data transfer controller (DTC) that stores results in memory without the CPU. It has eight external inputs A0 to A7, an internal temperature sensor on channel 10 and a VCC/2 divider on channel 11. The reference can be driven out on P1.4 (VREF+) and P1.3 (VREF-), or external references taken in on the same pins; the buffered output tolerates at most 100 pF on the pin. Its internal oscillator runs at 3.7 MHz to 6.3 MHz.

A 16-bit sigma-delta converter with a differential programmable gain amplifier (gain 1 to 32), a 1.2 V internal reference and internal channels for VCC sense and a temperature sensor. Inputs A0 to A4 are differential pairs on P1.0 to P1.7. The reference appears on P1.3 (VREF), where an external reference of 1.0 V to 1.5 V can be applied instead. A 100 nF capacitor on VREF is recommended to lower noise; with the reference output buffer on, 470 nF is required. The SD16_A needs AVCC of 2.5 V or more. The QFN version has separate analog and digital supply pins.
Setting a pin's analog enable bit (CAPD.x, ADC10AE.x or SD16AE.x) turns off its output driver and input Schmitt trigger so an analog voltage does not cause cross current in the input buffer.

The parts are programmed and debugged in the system through four-wire JTAG on P1.4 to P1.7 (selected by TEST) or through two-wire Spy-Bi-Wire on TEST/SBWTCK and RST/NMI/SBWTDIO; no external programming voltage is needed. The emulation logic is on chip. In JTAG mode the port pullups and pulldowns are off. TEST has an internal pulldown of 60 kΩ typical. Blowing the security fuse, by 6 V to 7 V on TEST for 1 ms with up to 100 mA, permanently disables JTAG, Spy-Bi-Wire and emulation access.
After reset the oscillator driver is connected to XOUT/P2.7. If the pin is used as an input, extra current flows until P2SEL.7 is cleared.
The RSA package's exposed pad is recommended to be tied to VSS and must be soldered to the board for thermal and mechanical reasons.

The TSSOP marking is F20xx (F20xxT for T versions), the PDIP marking the full MSP430F20xx (with T), and the QFN marking M430F over 20xx (with T). All packages are RoHS, NiPdAu finish (some QFN lots also SN). PDIP and TSSOP are MSL 1 at 260°C; QFN is MSL 1 or MSL 2 at 260°C depending on the order code. An enhanced-product version, MSP430F2013-EP, is offered for defense, aerospace and medical uses.
